## R Tidyverse vs. Python Pandas vs. Python Polars

This reference table outlines the structural translation layer between traditional data manipulation frameworks and modern, high-performance query engines.

 > <sub>Note: Operations in <span class="matrix-blue">blue</span> are global, console operations

| Operation | R (dplyr / tidyverse) | Pandas Method Chain | Polars Expression Chain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Filter Rows** | `filter(col > 50)` | `.query("amount > 50")` | `.filter(pl.col("amount") > 50)` |
| **Filter Multiple (AND)** | `filter(A > 10, B == "X")` | `.query("A > 10 and B == 'X'")` | `.filter(pl.col("A") > 10, pl.col("B") == "X")` |
| **Mutate Columns** | `mutate(fee = amt * 0.02)` | `.assign(fee = lambda df: ...)` | `.with_columns(fee = pl.col("amt") * 0.02)` |
| **Select Columns** | `select(col1, col2)` | <code><span class="matrix-red">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>[[&quot;col1&quot;,&nbsp;&quot;col2&quot;]]</code> | `.select("col1", "col2")` |
| **Select "All BUT" Columns**| `select(!c(col2, col5))` | <code>.loc[:, ~<span class="matrix-red">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>.columns<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;.isin([&quot;col2&quot;,&nbsp;&quot;col5&quot;])]</code> | `.select(pl.all().exclude(["col2", "col5"]))` |
| **Sort Rows** | `arrange(col1)` | <code>.sort_values(by&nbsp;=&nbsp;&quot;col1&quot;)</code> | `.sort("col1")` |
| **Optimize Top Rows** | `slice_max(amt, n = 3)` | `.nlargest(3, "amt")` | `.top_k(3, by = "amt")` |
| **Group Data** | `group_by(category)` | `.groupby("category")` | `.group_by("category")` |
| **Aggregate** | `summarise(rev = sum(amt))` | `.agg(rev = ("amt", "sum"))` | `.agg(pl.col("amt").sum().alias("rev"))` |
| **Type Cast** | `mutate(col = as.numeric(col))` | <code>.assign(col3&nbsp;=&nbsp;lambda&nbsp;df:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;pd.to_numeric(df[&quot;col3&quot;],<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;errors&nbsp;=&nbsp;&quot;coerce&quot;))</code> | `.cast(pl.Float64, strict = False)` |
| **Clean Strings** | `mutate(col = str_to_lower(col))` | <code>.assign(col3&nbsp;=&nbsp;lambda&nbsp;df:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;df[&quot;col3&quot;].str.lower())</code> | `.with_columns(pl.col("col3").str.to_lowercase())` |
| **Rename** | `rename_with(~ str_to_lower(str_trim(.)))` | <code>.rename(columns&nbsp;=&nbsp;lambda&nbsp;c:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;c.strip().lower())</code> | <code>.rename({c: c.strip().lower() for c in<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;<span class="matrix-red">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>.collect_schema().names()})</code> |
| **Conditional Assignment: Columns** | <code>mutate(col&nbsp;=&nbsp;if_else(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;A&nbsp;>&nbsp;50,&nbsp;"High",&nbsp;"Low"))</code> | <code>.assign(col&nbsp;=&nbsp;lambda&nbsp;df:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;np.where(df[&quot;A&quot;]&nbsp;>&nbsp;50,&nbsp;&quot;High&quot;,&nbsp;&quot;Low&quot;))</code> | <code>.with_columns(col&nbsp;=&nbsp;pl.when(pl.col(&quot;A&quot;)&nbsp;>&nbsp;50)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;.then(pl.lit(&quot;High&quot;))<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;.otherwise(pl.lit(&quot;Low&quot;)))</code> |
| **Conditional Reassignment: Global** | <code>mutate(across(everything(),&nbsp;&#x5C;(entry)&nbsp;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;if_else(entry&nbsp;==&nbsp;-99,&nbsp;NA,&nbsp;entry)))</code><br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<span class="matrix-red"><sub>*See note in "Object Dependency"</span> | `.mask(lambda x: x == -99, np.nan)` | <code>.with_columns(pl.all().when(pl.all()&nbsp;==&nbsp;-99)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;.then(None).otherwise(pl.all()))</code> |
| **Row Filtering** | <code>filter(!mad_thresh(pick(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;where(is.numeric))))</code> | <code>.loc[lambda&nbsp;df:&nbsp;~mad_thresh(df<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;.select_dtypes(include&nbsp;=<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;[&quot;float64&quot;,&nbsp;&quot;int64&quot;]))]</code> | <code>.filter(~pl.any_horizontal(<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;mad_thresh(cs.numeric())))</code> |
| **Dynamic Column Selection** <br><sub>*(Filter layout by data types/selectors)* | <code>select(where(is.character)&nbsp;&#x7C;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;any_of("v_id"))</code> | <code>.loc[:,&nbsp;lambda&nbsp;df:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;df.columns.isin(["v_id"])]</code> | <code>.select(cs.string()&nbsp;&#x7C;&nbsp;<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;pl.col("v_id"))</code> |
| **Function Parameter Injection** <br><sub>*(Pass specific column name into custom tools)* | `mutate(new = {{ col_var }})` | `.with_columns(pl.col(col_var))` | `.assign(new = lambda x: x[col_var])` |
| <span class="matrix-blue">**Limit Column Length**</span> | <code><span class="matrix-blue">options(pillar.width&nbsp;=&nbsp;100)</span></code> | <code><span class="matrix-blue">pd.set_option(&quot;display.max_colwidth&quot;,&nbsp;25)</span></code> | <code><span class="matrix-blue">pl.Config.set_fmt_str_lengths(25)</span></code> |
| <span class="matrix-blue">**Float / Coordinate Precision**</span> | <code><span class="matrix-blue">options(digits&nbsp;=&nbsp;4)</span></code> | <strong>Pandas:</strong><br><code><span class="matrix-blue">pd.set_option("display.precision",&nbsp;4)</span></code><br><strong>GeoPandas:</strong><br><code><span class="matrix-blue">gpd.options.display_precision&nbsp;=&nbsp;4</span></code> | <code><span class="matrix-blue">pl.Config.set_fmt_float_precision(4)</span></code> |

---

### Multi-Engine Type Casting Alignment

While some operations have a global scope and can either be piped (R) or accessed as a dataframe method (Python) directly, others must be directed using either a scoping function (R) or a specific object/class-method invocation (Python). The general syntax for how to deal with these operations that require further direction are listed below.


| Engine | Pipeline Syntax | Scope Handler | Vector Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **R (Tidyverse)** | `df |> mutate(col = str_to_lower(col))` | `mutate()` opens the data frame | `str_to_lower()` transforms the vector |
| **Python (Pandas)** | `df.assign(col = df["col"].str.lower())` | `.assign()` evaluates key-words | `.str.lower()` transforms the Series | 
| **Python (Polars)** | `df.with_columns(pl.col("col").str.to_lowercase())` | `.with_columns()` opens the context | `.str.to_lowercase()` transforms the expression |


### Object Dependency & Expressive Coupling

While most of the above syntax are object-agnostic, there are a few above that *do* require a direct reference to the parent object. Such exceptions are listed with the specific parent reference in <span class="matrix-red">[red bold text]</span>. I will also list such exceptions below.

* <code><span class="matrix-red">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>[[&quot;col1&quot;,&nbsp;&quot;col2&quot;]]</code>
* <code>.loc[:, ~<span class="matrix-red">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>.columns.isin([&quot;col2&quot;,&nbsp;&quot;col5&quot;])]</code>
* <code>.rename({c: c.strip().lower() for c in <span class="matrix-red">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>.collect_schema().names()})</code>
* *Alternative R syntax for  "Conditional Assignment: Global": <code><span class="matrix-red">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>[<span class="matrix-red">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>&nbsp;==&nbsp;-99]&nbsp;<-&nbsp;NA</code>



### Critical Structural Architecture Notes

#### 1. The Polars Multi-Argument Shortcut (Dropping `[...]`)
In both `.filter()` and `.agg()`, Polars allows you to completely drop Python list brackets `[...]` and pass expressions as simple comma-separated arguments. 

* **Filters:** Commas are automatically interpreted as a logical `AND`. This completely eliminates the nightmare of nesting matching parentheses like `((condition_a) & (condition_b))`.
* **Aggregations:** Dropping the list bracket allows you to cleanly list each metric on a brand-new vertical line, maximizing scannability.

#### 2. The `.top_k()` Heap-Select Shift
When your goal is finding the highest or lowest values in a pipeline, break the traditional habit of running `.sort().head()`. 

Using `.top_k()` triggers Polars' internal **Heap-Select algorithm**. Instead of using heavy computational overhead to sort millions of rows just to discard 99% of them, Polars dynamically tracks only the top records at the file-scan level, preserving memory and execution speed.

#### 3. The Polars Expression Console Context Rule
The internal engine differentiates strictly between mutating a whole dataframe and evaluating a column slice. 
* If the background parser knows you are modifying a DataFrame/LazyFrame object, your execution environment is safe.
* If you attempt to edit text downstream of an active, unclosed `pl.col()` expression without assigning it proper structural scope, the engine loses track of its columnar position and will throw an immediate error.

#### 4. Critical Pipeline "Gotchas"

* **Contagious NaN Values**: Vectorized statistical engines (like `np.median`) propagate `NaN` values across entire arrays. Rule: Always sequence structural drops (`.dropna()`) immediately before calling statistical outlier masks inside the chain to prevent the total collapse of the filter window.
* **Method Constraints**: Unlike `.loc[]` and `.assign()`, native operations like `.dropna(subset=...)` do not support raw callable inputs. Use explicit external dataframe references when mapping schema masks, or pass the block through a `.pipe()` layer to enforce encapsulation.
